featureRef: 4.11 Refunding an unused credit on withdrawal
name: Return an unused credit to a family who leaves the school
priorityReason: A credit is normally used against the next bill. Once a family leaves there is no next bill, and the school is holding money that is not its own.

goal.capability: to return an unused credit to a household that has left
goal.outcome: the family gets their money back and the school stops holding a liability it can never discharge against a bill

secondaryActors.involvement: Approves the payment out. Money leaving the school is not School Admin's decision.
Confirms no further charge is due from the household before the refund is raised.
Receives the refund and acknowledges it.

externalActors.involvement: Settles the refund where it is paid by transfer or cheque rather than in cash.

additional.description: A student is marked as left while a credit balance is still held against their household.
A periodic check lists households holding an unused credit with no enrolled child (BR-11).

preconditions.condition: A credit balance is held against the family code and has not been used.

establishedBy.name: Crediting a wrong charge already paid

preconditions.condition: Every child in the household has withdrawn, or is withdrawing, so no next bill exists to apply the credit to (BR-2).

establishedBy.name: View and maintain the student record

postConditions: The refund has been paid and the credit balance against the family code is discharged, so the school no longer carries the liability.
The payment out went through the ordinary voucher route, so it appears in the books alongside every other payment the school makes.
Both the credit and the refund that discharged it are recorded against the family code, so the money can be traced from where it arose to where it went.
The household's account reads zero, with no credit and no outstanding charge.
The family has been told the refund was made, by what method and on what date.
The original credit and the original charge behind it are still in place. Nothing has been deleted.
A part refund leaves the remainder still held, so the family can be paid the rest later.
Where a charge was still outstanding, it was settled from the credit first and only the balance was returned.

businessRules.rule: A refund is the only route by which a credit becomes cash. Everywhere else a credit is applied to the next bill, and this exists because a family who has left has no next bill.

A refund is raised only where the household has no enrolled child. While any child remains, the credit is applied to their bill instead, since that is what the family expects and what costs the school nothing.
Any charge still outstanding against the household is settled from the credit first, and only the balance is returned. The school does not hand back money and then chase the same family for a debt.
The amount refunded may not exceed the credit remaining after outstanding charges are settled. There is no route by which a refund creates a debt.

The payment out is raised through the ordinary voucher route for money leaving the school. No separate refund mechanism exists, so a refund appears in the books alongside every other payment the school makes.
A refund is raised by one person and approved by the Principal or Director. Money leaving the school is not School Admin's decision, and Accounts cannot both raise and grant it.
The refund is paid to the guardian on the household record, not to whoever asks for it. A person walking in claiming a refund is not evidence of who paid.
A part refund is permitted. The remainder stays held against the family code and can be paid later.
The refund is recorded as paid on the date the money actually left, not the date it was approved. The two differ whenever a cheque waits for collection.
The credit is discharged by exactly what was refunded, so the household account reads correctly afterwards and cannot be refunded twice.
Households holding an unused credit with no enrolled child are surfaced periodically. A credit nobody remembers is a liability the school carries indefinitely.
The original credit and the charge behind it stay in place. A refund is an additional entry, never a deletion.

transitions.condition: Authorised. The payment voucher is raised (BR-5, BR-6).

basicFlow.userAction: Identifies a household holding an unused credit where the student has withdrawn.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Lists households with a credit held, their children's status and any outstanding charge.

basicFlow.navigation: Unused credits → Household account → Raise refund
basicFlow.userAction: Confirms the balance and that no further charge is due from the household.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Checks no child remains enrolled and settles any outstanding charge from the credit before offering a refund amount.

basicFlow.navigation: Raise refund → Method, payee and reason
basicFlow.userAction: Selects the method and payee, states the reason, and submits the refund.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Checks the payee is the guardian on the household record, and sets the refund to Awaiting approval.

basicFlow.userAction: Reviews the refund and approves the payment out.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records the approval. No other role can give it.
Raises the payment voucher through the ordinary route for money leaving the school.

basicFlow.userAction: Records that the money has actually left, on the date it did.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Posts the entry, clears the liability and discharges the credit by exactly the amount refunded.
Tells the family the refund was made, by what method and on what date.

alternateFlows.condition: A charge is still outstanding against the household
alternateFlows.behaviour: The outstanding charge is settled from the credit first and only the balance is offered, so the school does not hand money back and then chase the same family for a debt (BR-3).

alternateFlows.condition: A younger sibling is still enrolled
alternateFlows.behaviour: No refund is raised. The credit is applied to that child's next bill instead, which is what the family expects and costs the school nothing (BR-2).

alternateFlows.condition: The family wants only part of the credit returned
alternateFlows.behaviour: A part refund is raised and the remainder stays held against the family code, payable later (BR-8).

alternateFlows.condition: The Principal does not accept the refund
alternateFlows.behaviour: It returns to Accounts with a written reason. The credit is untouched and still held.

alternateFlows.condition: The family re-enrols before the refund is paid
alternateFlows.behaviour: The refund is cancelled and the credit stays held, ready to reduce the new bill.

alternateFlows.condition: A periodic check finds a long-held credit with no enrolled child
alternateFlows.behaviour: The household is surfaced for a refund, since a credit nobody remembers is a liability the school carries indefinitely (BR-11).

exceptions.condition: The amount exceeds the credit remaining

exceptions.condition: The payee is not the guardian on the household record
exceptions.messageShown: A refund is paid to the guardian on the record. Correct the record first if the guardian has changed.

exceptions.condition: Accounts attempt to approve their own refund
exceptions.messageShown: Only the Principal or Director can approve a refund.

exceptions.condition: A School Admin attempts to approve
exceptions.messageShown: Only the Principal or Director can approve money leaving the school.

exceptions.systemResponse: The refund stays Approved and unpaid, and the credit is not discharged. Nothing is left half-done.
exceptions.messageShown: The refund could not be recorded as paid. The credit is still held.

exceptions.condition: A refund is marked paid twice
exceptions.systemResponse: The second is refused. The credit is discharged exactly once (BR-10).

departures.requirement: The person who raises a refund can never be the person who approves it, and approval sits with the Principal because money is leaving the school.
A credit is discharged exactly once by exactly the amount refunded, even where a refund is marked paid twice.
Credits held against households with no enrolled child are reported, so the school does not carry a liability nobody remembers.
Refunds, their vouchers and their acknowledgements are retained 7 years as financial records.

openQuestions.question: How long after a family leaves should an unused credit be refunded rather than held?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and it decides when the periodic check should surface a household.

openQuestions.question: What happens to a credit a family never claims and cannot be contacted about?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified. Unclaimed money has a legal position that needs deciding.

openQuestions.question: May a family ask for a refund before withdrawing, if they simply want their money back?
openQuestions.assumption: Not under this use case. Confirm the school will refuse it.

openQuestions.question: Is a signed acknowledgement required for a cash refund?
openQuestions.assumption: Offered but not required. It probably should be for cash.

openQuestions.question: Where siblings are at different branches, which branch pays the refund?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and family codes may span branches.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: money
conventionsApplied.rule: All monetary values are stored as fixed-point decimals in the smallest currency unit, never as floating point. Displayed as PKR with a thousands separator and two decimal places. Rounding is half-up at the line.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: attachments
conventionsApplied.rule: Uploaded files are limited to 10 MB and to PDF, JPG, PNG, DOCX and XLSX unless a use case states otherwise. File type is validated by content, not by extension.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
